title: Selected Bibliography: Heidegger and Rhetoric

abbreviations.full_form: Martin Heidegger's collected works (Gesamtausgabe), followed by volume number

compiler_note_section_a: The term 'rhetoric' can be found in at least eight places. Seven of those come from the Marburg period, when Heidegger makes regular reference to Greek rhetoric from a philosophical perspective. In order to get a full picture of Heidegger's relationship to rhetoric, one must consider rhetoric more broadly as the everydayness of being-with-one-another (Alltäglichkeit des Miteinanderseins). See indexes compiled by Petkovšek and Feick/Ziegler.

'Leitfaden' für die Bestimmung der Stellung der 'wissenschaftliche[n] Begriffsbildung im Dasein des Menschen' (123f)

cross_pipeline_summary.bcap_pipeline: All 8 Section A loci point to BCAP-relevant texts. BIB-A-1 (Wahrsein und Dasein 1923/24) and BIB-A-2 (GA 18) are the BCAP-source texts; BIB-A-6 (GA 22 SS 1926) is the closest sequel.
cross_pipeline_summary.bt_pipeline: BIB-A-7 (Sein und Zeit §§29-30, §68b) is the BT-pipeline anchor for Befindlichkeit + Furcht. This is the volume's single most-cited Heidegger passage (Hyde, Gross, Struever, Kisiel).
cross_pipeline_summary.aristotle_pipeline: BIB-A-1 cites Aristotle's Rhetoric 1.2-3; BIB-A-7 cites Rhetoric 2.5 (1382a 20–1383b11). All loci reference the Greek text that the Aristotle pipeline catalogs.
cross_pipeline_summary.section_b_overall: Section B (the 1922-1925 working corpus around GA 18) is mostly outside existing pipelines except BIB-B-4/B-5/B-6/B-8 which prefigure BT's temporality + Dilthey-genealogy.

ocr_notes: Source PDF has moderate OCR noise (PUBLISHED → PlJBLISHED; German umlauts garbled; italicized titles broken). All entries have been normalized to standard scholarly form; spelling corrections applied silently. The 10-entry count for Section B (vs Phase 0's anticipated 12) reflects the explicit PDF layout — the Phase 0 anticipation may have counted entries differently (e.g., distinguishing 'Kasseler Post' as separate from the main Kassel lectures entry).
